claims.text: Refractory HEAs modified to contain low-activation alloying elements are suitable as structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Selecting specific alloying elements in refractory HEAs will reduce activation levels.
Refractory HEAs containing the selected elements will maintain high-temperature stability.
The proposed intervention is to replace or modify conventional HEA alloying elements with low-activation elements.
Fusion-reactor plasma-facing components operate in high-temperature environments.
The choice of alloying elements controls the activation properties of the HEA.
The choice of alloying elements controls the mechanical stability of the HEA at high temperature.
Modified HEAs will have lower activation levels than standard refractory HEAs containing conventional alloying elements.
Modified HEAs will retain or improve high-temperature mechanical stability relative to standard refractory HEAs.
Conventional refractory HEAs may have higher activation levels than low-activation-element-modified HEAs.
The effects of specific alloying-element changes on activation and mechanical properties are not fully known.
